dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Before writing any code, reads the template, lists data/tokenizer, checks GPU, and probes the actual .bin files — discovers uint16 tokens with a 256-int32 header, 137.6M train / 294K val tokens, vocab 8192. Confirms data-format assumptions empirically rather than guessing.

Derives the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope up front: rejects a 77.9M-param model (~83MB compressed), iteratively resizes to fit under 32MB, repeatedly tests int8+zlib compressed checkpoint size (27.15MB→29.47MB→30.5MB), treating the byte cap as a concrete design constraint that shapes architecture.

Probes the tokenizer to compute avg bytes/token (5.078) to correctly convert the logged bits/token into the grader's bits-per-byte metric vs the 0.983 target — resolving a subtle contract detail rather than assuming.

Deliberately maps the load/forward contract: tests load_model_for_verification, verifies loss equals F.cross_entropy of the logits, runs an OOD probe confirming logits depend on position, and proactively adds the second load path (dequantize_state_dict_int8) for robustness against 'either' interface.
Final verification confirms all contract facets: forward signatures, OOD/position dependence, 24.6MB < 32MB, both loading paths present — showing sustained contract awareness through to submission.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it not only read the spec/template and identified shard format, vocab, and the 32MB cap, but deliberately mapped the full contract — both load paths, the loss==cross_entropy requirement, int8 dequant round-trip, and position-dependent logits — and probed the actual data and tokenizer (bytes/token conversion) to confirm assumptions, matching anchor 8 strongly. It also derived the size/quantization design envelope up front and implemented both load paths (anchor-10 traits), but never explicitly reasoned about decimal-vs-binary MB, the (args, model) tuple return form, or bf16-noise stability, so it stops short of a full 10.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: Before committing to full training, the agent repeatedly instantiated the model on CPU and checked compressed checkpoint size against the 32MB budget as an explicit gate — rejected a 77.9M-param model (83.6MB) and iteratively resized to ~30M/30.5MB. A genuine size-under-budget milestone that de-risked before training.

Verified the int8 quantize + zlib save/load roundtrip worked (27.8M→27.15MB, load succeeds) prior to launching real training — a saves/loads/quantizes-under-budget done-check consistent with anchor 5.

Only after the size/roundtrip gate did it launch the (near-max-capacity) training run and monitor val_bpb trajectory. It never trained a tiny model first nor measured a baseline val_bpb before the big run; capacity was fixed at max up front rather than scaled after locking correctness.

Grader-interface load_model_for_verification, forward-contract equality, and OOD probe were verified DURING the big training run, not as a pre-scaling gate — so contract correctness was not locked before capacity commitment (falls short of anchor 8).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed clear phasing beyond implicit ordering: explore → build model with an explicit size-under-32MB gate and a save/load/quantize roundtrip check → train → monitor val_bpb, with rough per-phase criteria (anchor 5). However it skipped the tiny-model end-to-end baseline and never measured a baseline val_bpb before scaling, and it verified the grader-load/forward contract only mid-training rather than locking contract+size correctness before capacity choice — so it does not reach the concrete-gate, contract-before-scaling structure of anchor 8. This lands squarely at 5.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: Repeatedly ran save/load roundtrip of the int8-quantized+zlib checkpoint and measured compressed size vs the 32MB cap (27.15MB, 29.47MB, 30.5MB), resizing the model to fit — genuine size + dequant roundtrip verification, not just 'file saves'.
Calibrated the proxy: computed avg bytes/token (5.078) to convert measured bits/token to bits/byte (~0.86 bpb) and explicitly reasoned about margin below the 0.983 threshold.

Ran a verification script through the exact grader entry point load_model_for_verification on the saved .ptz, confirming 'loss matches cross_entropy exactly' (loss/logits contract) and an OOD probe (loss_real < 0.7*loss_arange, real-LM/content dependence), plus size 24.9MB.

Noticed only one load path existed and added dequantize_state_dict_int8 as the second grader path for robustness, but verified only via grep that both functions exist — did not independently exercise the GPT+dequantize path.
Re-ran load_model_for_verification on the checkpoint immediately before finalizing and confirmed all checks (contract, OOD, size, both paths present) as a pre-submission gate.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent verified end-to-end through the real grader entry point (load_model_for_verification), asserted loss equals cross_entropy of returned logits, ran a real-LM/content-dependence probe, exercised int8 dequant roundtrips, and treated local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with explicit margin to 0.983 — matching the level-8 anchor. It stops short of 10: there was no standalone automated harness mirroring BOTH load paths with shifted-pass bpb run as a gate across iterations, the GPT+dequantize path was added but never independently tested, and position-dependence was not explicitly asserted.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: Set up val_bpb eval every 500 steps and tracked the trajectory (7.05→5.71→5.23→5.00) against the 0.983 target, verifying checkpoint size dropping in parallel.

Computed per-interval improvement (1.34, 0.48, 0.23), recognized decline slowing (plateau), and extrapolated steps-to-target — deciding whether to continue or restart with a larger model based on that read.

Corrected its done-vs-remaining model by realizing the metric was bits/token not bits/byte, computing avg bytes/token (5.078) to recalibrate to ~0.90 bpb < target — a deliberate re-anchoring of progress against threshold.

Tracked compute budget (~475K tok/s, step 9200/30000) and comfortable margin (0.83 vs 0.983), then deliberately stopped training early citing diminishing returns rather than grinding to a fixed step count.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an accurate, continuously-updated picture of the val_bpb trajectory versus the 0.983 target and versus remaining compute, distinguished plateau from under-training, and made stop/continue/restart decisions from that read rather than fixed step counts — squarely anchor 8. It also caught and corrected a metric misinterpretation, showing genuine done-vs-remaining reasoning. It does not reach 10 because monitoring centered on a single successful run rather than sustained reallocation across many runs under proxy-noise margins.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: Diagnosed 77.9M-param model → 83.6MB overshoot of the 32MB cap and made a reasoned architecture cut to ~24M params rather than re-running the same config — a size-binding-constraint correction.

Measured compressed checkpoint (27.15MB) and deliberately grew the model back up (30M→31M params, 30.5MB) to fill the byte budget with headroom — capacity-vs-size frontier trading, an 8-level flavored move on the size axis.

Three distinct crash-driven corrections each with root-cause diagnosis: torch.compile failure (no compiler)→eager mode; CUDA OOM (4GB logits)→smaller batch; in-place tanh autograd break→standard softcap. Changed the right lever each time, never repeated the same failing run.

Diagnosed that the val_bpb readout was bits/token not bits/byte, computed the 5.078 bytes/token conversion, and correctly reinterpreted the signal (already passing at ~0.90 bpb) instead of triggering an unnecessary architecture change — strong evidence-based diagnosis.

Since the single real training run converged and passed comfortably, the bpb frontier was never contested; the agent monitored and eventually stopped, so no falsified-run-driven, compounding bpb corrections were demonstrated (below the 10 anchor).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently diagnosed the binding constraint before acting — size overshoot, OOM, compile failure, autograd break, and a mislabeled metric — and changed the correct lever with re-checks, exceeding the level-5 'reasoned single-lever change' bar. The deliberate measure-then-grow-to-fill-the-byte-budget behavior is genuine capacity-vs-size frontier trading characteristic of level 8. However it falls short of a full 8/10 because the quantization scheme was never traded for accuracy and, critically, the bpb axis was never actually contested (the first run passed), so there were no compounding, falsified-run-driven bpb corrections. This places the observed behavior at a 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Before any training run, repeatedly used cheap compute — py_compile syntax checks, CPU model-size estimation, save/load roundtrip tests — to validate the contract and byte cap, matching the level-5 'reserve cheap compute before committing' behavior.

Roughly sized the run to the goal ('30M params, 20-30k iterations, ~70 min at 475K tok/s'), but this was generic capacity reasoning, not an empirical probe of steps-needed-to-threshold — so short of anchor 10.
Monitored val_bpb trajectory and extrapolated steps to reach 0.983 ('would require ~4500 steps'), showing allocation reasoning informed by incoming results.

Once the checkpoint already crossed the threshold with margin (~0.83 bpb at ~step 9200 of 30K), it debated stop-vs-continue and killed training early to finalize a verified submission — a genuine reallocation, not spending the full pre-planned budget.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it reserved cheap compute for contract/size validation before the main run and roughly sized the run to the goal, then adjusted allocation mid-run by extrapolating the val trajectory and stopping early once the threshold was safely crossed. It falls short of anchor 8 because there was no distinct targeted-tuning phase, and short of 10 because the main-run size was set by generic reasoning rather than small informative capacity/step probes. This places it between 5 and 8, at 6.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
